title: China's Xi Jinping to visit India with 400-member delegation for Brics: Report
content: Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to arrive in New Delhi for the upcoming BRICS summit next month. Accompanied by a robust delegation of around 400 officials, this visit marks a significant increase from his last attendance. This diplomatic mission comes at a crucial time as India and China aim to mend their relationship following past border conflicts.

title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hits back with 2 wickets in 4 balls in Duleep Trophy - WATCH
content: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi had faced only six balls and scored eight runs before being dismissed by North East Zone pacer Bishworjit Konthoujam in East Zone's first innings. But he responded with the ball, needing only eight deliveries to take his first wicket.

title: Dead denied dignity: Man’s body ‘floated’ on tied drums through Rewa floodwaters
content: Villagers in Rouli, Rewa district, used drums to create a raft for a deceased person. The body was transported from the hospital to the home across floodwaters. This incident has led to accusations of insensitivity against the local panchayat. Officials have denied these allegations and stated boats were arranged. A video of the event surfaced online, causing public outrage and calls for an inquiry.

title: CEO of world's biggest robot firm admits that robots years away from ‘ChatGPT moment’
content: Wang Xingxing, the CEO of Unitree, emphasizes the necessity for further advancements in humanoid robotics. He forecasts that we might witness a significant breakthrough in the next five to ten years. For robots to become truly functional, they must execute eighty percent of their tasks through voice or text commands.

title: Sugar prices cool 18% after hitting record high, ex-mill rates fall to Rs 55 per kg
content: Following a surge in sugar prices to unprecedented levels last week, the market is now experiencing a decline. Government interventions aimed at curbing hoarding and speculation have contributed to this stabilization. Ex-mill sugar rates have seen a substantial decrease, and additional cuts are anticipated. Although predictions for domestic sugar output are lower, current stock levels remain adequate. Consumers are still eager for reductions in both wholesale and retail pricing.

title: 'When will we stop telling women what to wear': Sanon to Kangana over Rakhi remarks
content: Kriti Sanon recently responded to criticism surrounding her outfit in a Rakshabandhan commercial. She passionately articulated that the true essence of the festival is rooted in emotions rather than clothing preferences. Sanon challenged the norm of judging women based on their wardrobe choices, insisting that cultural values and traditions are founded in one's heart. Meanwhile, her film 'Cocktail 2' debuted in June 2026.

title: Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan’s $125m school to shut after 10 yrs
content: The Primary School, a tuition-free institution for low-income families, has closed its doors after a decade. Funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative ceased, prompting the board's unanimous decision to shut down. While offering extensive support services, the school's academic results did not meet state benchmarks. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative is providing financial support for the transition and educational savings accounts.

title: 'An unfortunate racket': As India nears 100th GM, is expensive coach a must?
content: As India nears its 100th Grandmaster, veteran GM Pravin Thipsay questions the booming coaching industry, arguing that expensive training is often unnecessary and independent thinking matters more. While he calls the ecosystem an “unfortunate racket”, Grandmaster Aaryan Varshney offers a counterpoint, saying guidance remains crucial in the computer era. With inputs from Grandmasters, the story examines whether aspiring players really need to hire an expensive coach to become a GM.

title: Gold mine that produced 41 million ounces now houses America's deepest lab
content: A former gold mine in South Dakota has been transformed into a major underground science facility. The Homestake Mine once produced about 41 million ounces of gold and 9 million ounces of silver, but today its tunnels are used to study some of the Universe’s biggest mysteries. Scientists conduct experiments searching for dark matter, neutrinos and rare radioactive decay, while also researching microbes, geology and geothermal energy. Located 4,850 feet underground, the Sanford Underground Research Facility shows how a site once built for mining has found a new purpose in scientific discovery.

title: World’s largest battery-powered plane X1 completes maiden flight, uses just $5 electricity
content: Heart Aerospace's X1 electric jet has successfully completed its first flight in New York, soaring for an impressive twenty-seven minutes on battery power alone. The company is excited about their hybrid-electric ES-30 model, projected to make its debut in commercial service by 2031. This innovation has the potential to transform airline operations, offering substantial reductions in costs while promoting an eco-friendlier approach to air travel.

title: Overnight raid near Haiti capital kills around 50 - here is what happened
content: An assault in Kenscoff carried out by armed groups resulted in the deaths of at least forty-seven individuals, leaving twenty-two others injured. This area, which holds strategic importance overlooking routes to Haiti's capital, has seen many residents flee due to ongoing gang conflicts. In response, the government has committed to enhancing security measures and reestablishing order.

title: FSSAI crackdown: Food companies withdraw ‘100%’ and health claims after notices
content: India's food regulator FSSAI has taken action against several major food business operators. Companies like Amway India and Juza Foods have removed misleading claims from their products. These corrective actions follow notices issued over regulatory violations and consumer safety concerns. FSSAI's enforcement drive targets false advertisements and labelling discrepancies across the industry. Many businesses are now revising packaging and withdrawing problematic advertisements.

title: Delhi waterlogging fury: AAP councillors sail into MCD House with inflatable boat
content: AAP councillors brought an inflatable boat into the MCD House to protest severe city waterlogging.  The mayor adjourned the meeting for ten minutes due to the disruption.  Opposition councillors blamed the BJP for failing to address the serious waterlogging issue.  Discussions also covered drains, mosquito menace, and stray dogs during the meeting.  Serving councillors will receive medical treatment facilities under the CGHS scheme.

title: Surat fish market named after PM Modi sparks row
content: A new fish market in Surat faces controversy after being named after Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Some traders object, citing the Prime Minister's vegetarian diet and personal beliefs. The Surat Municipal Corporation clarified that the official naming process for the market is not yet complete. The Surat Fish Merchant Association claims they independently passed a resolution for the naming.

title: Delhi master plan 2047: 40 lakh affordable homes, land pooling and more
content: Delhi's Master Plan 2047 sets forth a comprehensive strategy for urban development, emphasizing both the revitalization of existing neighborhoods and the strategic expansion into undeveloped areas. The ambitious proposal aims to generate around forty lakh affordable housing units, supported by initiatives like land pooling to enhance urban infrastructure and ensure accessibility. Additionally, measures will be taken to regularize unauthorized colonies, providing greater security in property ownership.

title: Andhra family of 5 found dead in suicide pact at Srisailam pilgrim lodge
content: A heartbreaking event unfolded at the Vaddera Choultries in Srisailam, where five family members allegedly ended their lives. Three women were found lifeless in a bathroom, and two others were discovered hanging. They had been residing in the pilgrim accommodation for nearly a month. Staff members alerted the authorities upon noticing a disturbing smell from the room. Early indications suggest that significant financial difficulties may have driven this desperate decision.

title: TOI Impact: Flood-hit teachers to get alternative classrooms
content: In Bhind, Madhya Pradesh, the challenges of monsoon season are apparent as both teachers and students risk their safety to cross a swollen river to reach school. Following a viral video raising alarm, temporary classrooms were set up to address the urgent situation. The local authorities have announced that teachers will not incur penalties for absent e-attendance.

title: They left IIT to build billion-dollar companies: Why are alumni giving crores back?
content: IIT alumni are increasingly giving back to their alma maters through donations running into hundreds of crores, supporting medical schools, hostels, research, infrastructure and new academic institutions. Notable contributions include Rakesh Gangwal’s Rs 400 crore commitment to IIT Kanpur, Nandan Nilekani’s Rs 400 crore cumulative contribution to IIT Bombay and Dr Krishna Chivukula’s Rs 228 crore gift to IIT Madras. The trend reflects a growing reverse flow of wealth and expertise from successful graduates to India’s premier institutes.

title: Bengaluru techie earning Rs 1.8 lakh/month faces ICU emergency: 'I was crushing it'
content: A Bengaluru techie's emergency revealed income differs from accessible cash. His savings and investments were unavailable during a critical hospital admission. This incident highlighted the crucial need for liquid emergency funds before aggressive investing. Readers emphasized building emergency reserves and securing adequate health insurance coverage. High earnings alone do not ensure financial security; accessible funds are paramount.

title: 'They've fallen behind': Rahul Dravid on Team India's WTC final hopes
content: India have made a strong start to their ongoing series in Sri Lanka, leading 1-0 after winning the first Test in Galle by 165 runs. They have also taken control of the second Test after a big batting effort. Rahul Dravid feels the Sri Lanka series is an important first step, but India still have plenty of work to do.

title: Taxpayers in waist-deep water: Gurgaon's annual infrastructure betrayal
content: Gurgaon experienced significant disruption from recent monsoon rains. Major roads flooded, causing extensive traffic jams and stranding many commuters. Despite substantial infrastructure spending, the city faces recurring waterlogging issues. Civic body vacancies and a focus on symptoms hinder long-term resilience efforts. Changing rainfall patterns necessitate updated urban planning for future preparedness.

title: Just 0.1% of Rs 32kcr Kumbh funds could have saved over 100 schools: SC judge
content: Justice Prasanna Varale of the Supreme Court expressed alarm over the decline of Marathi-medium schools, emphasizing that enhanced government funding could have prevented the closure of several institutions. He pointed to the dire state of residential schools and reported student fatalities. Justice Varale asserted that education expenditure has not matched the increasing demands of students and called for the urgent modernization of schools with digital technologies to ensure quality education.

title: ‘Swimming pool at Talkatora Stadium’: AAP mocks BJP over waterlogging at Nabin event
content: The Aam Aadmi Party criticized the Bharatiya Janata Party after waterlogging occurred at Talkatora Stadium. BJP leaders had gathered there to flag off "Pavan Mati Kalash" processions for Sant Ravidas' birth anniversary. AAP MLA Kuldeep Kumar shared a video showing the event amidst flooded stadium grounds. He sarcastically congratulated Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta for the arrangements. The BJP stated the campaign aims to spread Sant Ravidas' teachings across society.

title: ‘System needs to take a pause’: Protest erupts at IIT Delhi days after student’s death
content: IIT Delhi students boycotted classes demanding justice for a deceased peer. They sought an independent probe into administrative failures and accountability for officials. Protesters also highlighted issues like academic project denial and inadequate support systems. The administration met with students, agreeing to consider compensation and an inquiry. Students condemned alleged moral profiling and called for systemic change.

title: ‘Demands unmet’: CJP calls march on Sept 5
content: The Cockroach Janta Party is set to stage a peaceful march to the Delhi Police headquarters, urging the government to uphold its promises made to youth who are protesting. Families of NEET students who tragically lost their lives will spearhead this demonstration, joined by survivors and fellow students.

title: CCTV shows BJP MLA's daughter slapping cop at Karnataka temple
content: CCTV footage shows an altercation between an MLA's daughter and a police sub-inspector. The incident occurred at a temple during celebrations and involved a dispute over temple entry. The daughter allegedly slapped the officer, who then retaliated, leading to intervention by others. Police registered an FIR against the daughter for assaulting a public servant. The MLA apologized for his daughter's conduct and called for a departmental inquiry.

title: 'Horrifying to the core': Gurgaon rain traps kids in school buses for over 7 hours
content: A severe monsoon downpour caused extensive flooding across Gurgaon roads on Monday. Many school buses were stranded for several hours, causing significant distress to students. Parents faced helplessness while tracking their children and exchanging updates on messaging groups. Some parents waded through deep water to reach their children from stranded buses. The incident highlighted the city's recurring infrastructure failures during heavy rainfall.

title: Why Trump may have to target China to make its Iran 'economic D-Day' work
content: China is the biggest buyer of Iranian crude - around 90% of Iran’s oil exports flow to China. Will Trump’s secondary sanctions threat against any country aiding Iran economically reach China, or even have an impact?

title: Zeeshan Ansari: 'India A and IPL exposure has made me a better leg-spinner'
content: After years in the wilderness, Zeeshan Ansari's IPL and India A exposure has helped the leg-spinner understand his craft better, with the UP T20 league providing the breakthrough that revived his career.

title: 'Unprofessional': Sanjay Manjrekar slams Sri Lanka’s antics in Colombo
content: Sanjay Manjrekar expressed disappointment with Sri Lanka's conduct as the match neared its climax, deeming their reaction to the fading light as somewhat unprofessional and distracting. While India declared their first innings, Sri Lanka stumbled to 8/2. In contrast, Manjrekar commended India's determination to continue playing despite the rain, highlighting their dominant position going into the next phase of the game.

title: From 600 to 5,000 packages an hour: FedEx unveils $150 million Delhi cargo hub
content: FedEx will invest $150 million to build a new air cargo hub in Delhi. This facility will significantly increase package processing capacity at the airport. The hub aims to strengthen air cargo connectivity across North and East India. The Indian government is also focusing on developing cargo hubs and logistics networks. Construction work for the new FedEx facility is expected to begin shortly.

title: Ravi Teja’s ‘Irumudi’ lands in trouble as teachers’ federation objects to school scenes
content: Following its debut, the Telugu film 'Irumudi' has stirred controversy. The Andhra Pradesh Teachers Federation is voicing concerns over specific scenes, alleging that they unfavorably depict government schools and educators. In response, the federation has demanded the filmmakers cut these scenes and issue an apology. As of now, the team behind 'Irumudi' has not provided any public comment regarding these claims.

title: Sridhar Vembu on workplace culture: Why does initiative matter more than orders?
content: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has sparked a discussion on workplace culture by contrasting organisations where employees wait for instructions with those that encourage initiative. He argues that metrics and hierarchy can provide predictability but may discourage independent thinking, while initiative-driven workplaces can be chaotic and argumentative yet foster experimentation and ownership. For students and young professionals, Vembu’s observations highlight the importance of balancing structure with autonomy, accountability and the confidence to act independently.

title: 'Punishment that sends shiver down team': Vaughan on Carse nightclub incident
content: Brydon Carse is under investigation by the England and Wales Cricket Board after a nightclub incident resulted in his arrest. Consequently, he has been removed from the Test squad. Former captain Michael Vaughan insists that a severe punishment is necessary for Carse, as this incident is part of a troubling trend of off-field conduct among England players.

title: Watch: Man fined Rs 5,500 after girlfriend covers his car with 3,400 lipstick kisses
content: A Gwalior resident faced a fine after his car was covered in lipstick marks. His girlfriend applied thousands of kiss imprints, transforming the vehicle into a canvas. Traffic police identified the car from social media images and traced its owner. The extensive exterior modification violated vehicle appearance and road safety regulations. The car owner paid the fine and had the lipstick marks removed from his vehicle.

title: Dera chief Ram Rahim walks out of jail again, gets 21-day furlough in 17th release
content: Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh has received another 21-day parole from jail.  He is currently serving a 20-year sentence for rape convictions.  This marks his seventeenth parole release since 2020.  Prison rules allow convicts up to ten weeks of parole annually.  His repeated releases have drawn significant public scrutiny and attention.

title: Maharashtra cancels ‘oral’ appointments in Ministerial offices
content: In a circular, Chief Secretary Rajesh Aggarwal directed that all such officials and employees must be sent back to their parent offices by September 10

title: Keralam CM Satheesan extends Onam greetings, calls for ‘unity beyond caste and religion’
content: V.D. Satheesan said “every Onam celebration inspires resilience and self-confidence, reminding people that they are never alone, even during difficult times.”

title: Hanur shoot-out: Four cases of attacks on forest staff, anti-poaching camps transferred to CID
content: According to reports, 11 anti-poaching camps, staff quarters and government vehicles in the Cauvery and adjoining Male Mahadeshwara wildlife sanctuaries were either allegedly vandalised or damaged, with some camps blown up using explosives.

title: Govt. approves transfer of DRDO developed missile tech to Indian defence industry
content: The Defence Ministry said the move is an "important milestone" in promoting greater participation of the domestic industries in the defence ecosystem

title: How Onam bridges generations in Keralam: Elders, millennials and Gen Z share their stories
content: As Keralam celebrates Onam, the festival continues to mean different things to different generations, yet brings them all together

title: Video showing Karnataka BJP MLA’s daughter slapping woman police official at temple goes viral
content: An argument had broken out between the MLA’s daughter and the police officer over the former’s attempt to enter the temple’s sanctum sanctorum. Soon, the exchange turned physical.

title: Rahul Gandhi, Kharge write letter to PM Modi; asks for current census questionnaire to be cancelled
content: Mallikarjun Kharge shared the letter on X, which says a new questionnaire should be prepared based on a verified list of castes

title: After 540 days of protests, Karnataka CM invites those opposing Bidadi Township for talks
content: The move came after farmers brought their protest to Bengaluru’s Freedom Park and announced that they would lay siege to Vidhana Soudha.

title: Four India-based companies bear the brunt of U.S.’ Iran sanctions
content: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced ‘Operation Economic Outcast’, which essentially involved new sanctions that aim to block all potential sources of revenue for Iran

title: Thaimaman Thanga Mothiram scheme: Vault-like enclosures for gold ring storage at Tamil Nadu’s 107 CEmONC centres
content: The State Health Secretary has written to the Engineer-in-Chief and Chief Engineer (Buildings), Public Works Department (PWD) to put in place safety enclosures for the storage facilities at these centres.

title: Supreme Court dismisses Tarun Tejpal’s plea, directs him to surrender within two weeks
content: The State of Goa, represented by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, had insisted that Tarun Tejpal should surrender before his appeal is listed for hearing in the Supreme Court

title: Tejpal moves Supreme Court against sentence in rape case
content: The journalist’s appeal follows the State of Goa’s petition in the top court a few days ago for enhancement of his punishment to life imprisonment

title: SC declines to direct reopening of CBSE re-evaluation portal for Class 12 answer sheets
content: The bench said the portal was opened for all candidates for a specified period and reopening could trigger fresh claims

title: Tamil Nadu taking steps to distribute medicine for haemophilia patients: Health Minister in Assembly
content: The Minister said Emicizumab was used to treat Haemophilia A patients with Factor VIII inhibitor antibodies

title: Supreme Court’s Samadhan Samaroh 2026 concludes with over 1,600 cases resolved
content: The cases included matrimonial and property disputes, motor accident claims, land acquisition and compensation matters, tax cases, and service and labour disputes

title: DMK objects to Tamil Nadu Minorities Commission chairman Felix Gerald’s participation in TV debates
content: A DMK member raises issue in the Assembly saying Mr. Gerald, who holds a statutory post, should not abuse members of the Opposition in TV debates

title: Farmers from Parandur meet Tamil Nadu CM Vijay, thank him for scrapping airport project
content: As a gesture of gratitude, the villagers of Ekanapuram have decided to name a lane in their village as C. Joseph Vijay road

title: The bygone movie theatres of Chennai: a compilation
content: This is a collection of stories by The Hindu on the popular single screens and theatre complexes that are etched in the memories of cinephiles of Chennai city even years after they ceased existing.

title: Thaimaman Thanga Mothiram scheme in Tamil Nadu: Work orders issued to two jewellers for supply of gold rings
content: Joyalukkas and Kalyan Jewellers are expected to supply a total of 1,28,499 one-gram gold rings for a four-month period beginning from June

title: Tamil Nadu Health Minister clarifies on gold ring scheme tender
content: The Minister said there are two components in the scheme - one being the gold price and the other being charges including making charges, for packing, transportation, insurance, and BIS hallmarking. The tender was floated not for the gold rate but the other component (additional charges)

title: Madras High Court permits construction of 110 shops around Cuddalore Manjakuppam playground
content: Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan agree that the shops would serve as a compound wall for the playground

title: SEBI’s ITRI — a global test for India’s future-ready financial architecture | Explained
content: The IT Resilience Index seeks to measure the resilience of critical systems at market infrastructure institutions amid rising technology dependence in India’s capital markets

title: Romance, longing, life, and cinema on Chennai’s beaches
content: While one could argue that the LIC Building established the “big city” vibe and that Spencer Plaza represented Chennai’s “modern and capitalist” aspects, the beach has always been used to represent love and life

title: Sanskrit varsity Syndicate revokes decision on unsigned exam tabulation registers, orders probe into lapses
content: Preliminary assessment finds that officials did not record their signatures in exams held since 2018. Those who had put their signatures on tabulation register following Syndicate decision on July 17 included those who had retired from service

content: Several people sent SMS to phone number 1950 to know their part number and part name, to select the draft rolls

content: Journalist Abhishek Upadhyay’s plea claims that an FIR lodged against him by the Ghaziabad Police in an alleged road rage case was based on concocted allegations against him and was an attempt to harass him for his independent journalistic works

content: The proposals have to cover conservation approach, proposed tourism experience, revenue model, community participation and other aspects

title: Udhayanidhi demands high-level judicial inquiry into killing of three Tamils by Karnataka forest officials
content: Udhayanidhi wanted to know whether the Tamil Nadu government had written to Karnataka, seeking an explanation about the incident

content: These filled declaration forms, taken for "self-safety", will be kept in the church offices to be shown to government or police authorities, if asked

title: Madras city on the move: a compilation
content: On Madras Day, here is a collection of articles from The Hindu, reminiscing the various modes of public transport that made the city move

title: From celluloid to digital: the changing face of Chennai’s cinema industry
content: Over 84 years, Kodambakkam, the heart of Tamil cinema, has changed beyond recognition, and so has the Tamil film world. Surviving all odds, cinemas have evolved from a single projector and four intervals to the IMAX of today, while filmmaking has moved on from the expensive process of shooting on celluloid to embracing digital technology

title: Madras lingo on transportation
content: A traffic island becomes a roundtana, while Emden, the name of a German cruiser that bombed Madras in 1914, came to mean a bully or devious adversary. Tankuvar Arundudum — meaning you lose control of a situation — comes from tankuvaru, a Telugu term referring to a small piece of leather used to fasten the saddle to a horse. These are just some words and phrases used in and around Madras, which trace their origins to modes of transportation

title: When aircrafts took to the Madras skies on metal wings
content: D’Angelis’ maiden flight in 1910 set in motion the aviation history of Madras. From a record-making 27-hour flight from London to Madras in a de-Havilland Dove and a night land that left the pilots “trembling like a leaf” to an air taxi that flew all the way to Burma and Alagappa Chettiar’s Jupiter Airways, the skies above Madras have surely never seen a dull moment

title: Getting around Madras on autorickshaws
content: From numbering around 200 in 1973 to around 1 lakh in 2026, autorickshaws in the city have come a long way, but so too has the love-hate relationship the residents share with this ubiquitous mode of transport. But if you are in a hurry, the autorickshaw is your best bet to reach your destination, traffic rule violations and all

title: How buses became the lifeline of Madras
content: Packed to the point of tipping over, driven rashly, and battered all over, is how one would describe the MTC buses that ply in the city. While buses were in use in Madras since the 1920s, they really took off only after the tram service met its demise in 1953. Since then, they have become an integral feature of the city and a lifeline for millions

title: How bicycles, motorcycles took over the roads of Madras
content: Bicycles first came to Madras sometime in the 1880s, and at the time, they had a modest start, with there even being demands for a separate lane for cyclists. And while cycles were riding onward, two-wheelers of the motor variety, not so quietly, took to the roads. Brands such as Royal Enfield even set up manufacturing units in the region. To this day, two-wheelers number among the most convenient ways for getting around in the city

title: Hauling about the Madras city on trains
content: Madras was the first place in India where trains were introduced. In 1856, Royapuram became the terminus for a line that ran to Walajah Road. On the suburban side, the ball began rolling in the 1900s, and while the network grew, it never quite rivalled those in places such as Mumbai. Then came the MRTS, which never realised its full potential. At present, Metro Rail is the city’s latest attempt to get back on track

title: When yellow-black taxis cruised the roads of Madras
content: In the 1960s and 1970s, yellow taxis were a force to contend with in Madras. While this mode of transport was never as prolific as its contemporaries, it nonetheless had a presence, with the prepaid taxis at the airport being the chief representative. The yellow-black cab was gradually sidelined by services such as taxis on call and aggregator apps. By 2023, it has been reported that only 304 of them still ride around the city

title: The four key roads of Madras that originate from Fort St. George
content: Madras’ traffic movement is by and large planned on a network created by four great roads. Today, we know them as Rajaji Salai, Kamaraj Salai, EVR Periyar Salai, and Anna Salai, and each retaining their distinct identities. However, their focal point to this day remains Fort Saint George

title: Around Madras city in hand-pulled rickshaws
content: Hand-pulled rickshaws arrived in Madras early in the 20th Century from Japan, and quickly became a convenience despite its very apparent issues. These were later banned in 1973. Their role was replaced by the marginally better cycle rickshaw, which received a helping hand from MGR’s 1971 blockbuster Rickshawkaran

title: Aboard the tramway in Madras
content: When Madras’ first tramway took to the streets in the 1870s, it was horse-drawn. A little over two decades later, the city got its electric tramway system going, much before any other city in the country. Up until its demise in April 1953, the Madras Electric Tramways Company Limited was largely plagued by malfunctions, never once managing to turn a profit

title: Jolted about on carts drawn by oxen and horses in Madras
content: When animal-powered transportation was in its heyday in the Madras region, it came in multiple varieties. While businessmen preferred the fast-moving rekla, which were even used for races, the horse-drawn jhutkas, which became the first public transport of Madras, were in use as recent as 1969. At one point, these carts required a licence and were even exempt from taxes, at least the ones drawn by horses and bullocks

title: Masula boats and the fishermen who kept Madras afloat
content: Before the harbour came into being, arriving in Madras by ship meant making the last leg of the journey on masula boats. These boatmen, who were mostly fishermen from the coast along Madras, knew that they were a vital link in keeping the city’s trade alive and made full use of the opportunity. But by the late 1890s, their era had all but come to an end

title: 10 Bills passed in Karnataka Legislature without debate amid BJP protest on last day of session
content: Among the Bills was the controversial Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which allows 5% of park land to be sold, leased, gifted, exchanged or mortgaged for public utility projects undertaken by government departments, statutory authorities, government companies or local bodies

title: Of the time when people were carried in palanquins in Madras
content: Palanquins, the very word tracing its origins to the Sanskrit paryanka and the Tamil pallakku, were how the high and mighty got around Madras of the 17th and 18th Centuries. Even records of The East India Company contain details of hire charges of palanquin bearers, with rates higher than even hiring horses. Nowadays, this yesteryear means of transport is mainly consigned to museums

title: When Madras was walk-friendly
content: While it might not be the fastest mode of transport, it is one that most people can always rely on, not to mention the oldest mode known to humans. Then, there are some sights that can only be taken in when one is out and about on foot. While the city’s recent track record with walkability hasn’t been the greatest, that’s not to say that was always the case

title: OBC creamy layer judgment: Centre seeks exemption for 2025 and 2026 civil service examination recruitments
content: The Union government has noted that the implementation of this judgment will lead to a cascade of litigation from previous years’ candidates of not just civil service examination but also all other aspects of government recruitment

title: Madras High Court stops felling of rosewood trees on private lands
content: Justice N. Sathish Kumar and Justice K. Rajasekar said the reasons for recommending the repeal of the Tamil Nadu Rosewood Trees (Conservation) Act, 1994, defied logic

content: Special campaign to be conducted in areas reporting high numbers of ‘absent, shifted, duplicate, dead’ names

content: The students, many of whom were carrying the tricolour in their hands, jostled with the police and broke through barricades at the Dak Bungalow crossing

content: Mr. Mabu, the veena artist and maker, presented the miniature model of the traditional stringed musical instrument designed by him, to Mr. Radhakrishnan

content: Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu said the DGCA is holding discussions with stakeholders on further strengthening the drug-testing standards of pilots

content: The operation was carried out by Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) units, supported by CoBRA and RAF commandos along with Manipur Police, as part of the ongoing de-weaponisation drive in the state.

title: "Taken Out Of Context": Nitin Gadkari's Office On "Can't Work As Before" Remark
content: The Minister's office stated that he was speaking specifically about the Laxmanrao Mankar Trust and the comments were made in that context.

title: Despite Training 7.67 Crore Individuals, Outcomes Remain Uneven: Niti Aayog
content: NITI Aayog cites data shows that only 8.25% of graduates are employed in jobs aligned with their qualifications. Graduate unemployment is high at 13%.

content: While enforcement details of new US measures remain sketchy, the threat could still put several of Tehran's major trade partners, including China and India, on a collision course with America.

content: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India buckled after a tense March meeting with industry executives, who argued that such warning labels were confusing and ineffective
